n: Pursue love above all, and also seek spiritual gifts — especially prophecy, which blesses others directly.

f.g: Speak inspired messages that teach and testify, not only foretell.

n: A person speaking in a tongue no one understands talks to God, not to people. In the Spirit he speaks mysteries, but no one else benefits.

f.g: A language unknown to the hearers. (“Unknown” is added by the KJV translators.)

n: Prophecy speaks to people to build them up, encourage them, and comfort them.
Tongues build up only the speaker; prophecy builds up the whole congregation.
Paul values tongues, but prophecy is greater — unless the tongue is interpreted so the Church benefits.
If Paul came speaking only in tongues, what good would it do them? They need revelation, knowledge, prophecy, or teaching they can understand.
Even a flute or harp must play distinct notes, or no one can recognize the tune.
If a bugle gives an unclear signal, soldiers won’t know to prepare for battle.
Likewise, unless you speak words people understand, you’re just talking into the air.
There are many languages in the world, and every one carries meaning.
But if I don’t understand someone’s language, we are foreigners to each other.

f.g: Greek barbaros — a foreigner whose speech sounded like “bar-bar” to Greeks.

n: Since you’re eager for spiritual gifts, seek ones that strengthen the Church.
So whoever speaks in a tongue should pray for the gift to interpret.
When praying in a tongue, my spirit prays but my mind gets nothing from it.
So Paul will pray and sing both with the Spirit and with understanding — heart and mind working together.
Otherwise, how can someone who doesn’t understand say “Amen” to your prayer of thanks? Saying Amen means agreeing with what was said.

f.g: Hebrew for “so be it” or “truly” — a congregation’s affirmation.
An outsider or inquirer unfamiliar with the gift.

n: Your prayer may be fine, but it doesn’t help anyone else.
Paul thanks God that he speaks in tongues more than any of them — so he isn’t criticizing the gift itself.

f.g: Perhaps including Paul’s ability to preach in many languages.

n: But in church he’d rather say five words people understand than ten thousand in a tongue.
Grow up in your thinking. Be innocent as babies regarding evil, but mature in understanding.
Paul cites Isaiah: God warned Israel He would speak through foreign-speaking invaders, yet they still wouldn’t listen.

f.w: With men of other tongues and other lips

n: So tongues are a sign mainly to unbelievers, while prophecy blesses believers.
If outsiders walk in while everyone is speaking in tongues, they’ll think you’re out of your minds.
But if all are speaking inspired truth plainly, an unbeliever who comes in will feel convicted and examined by what he hears.
The secrets of his heart will be exposed, and he will fall down and worship God, declaring that God is truly among them.

f.w: God is in you of a truth

n: What should worship look like? Each person brings something — a hymn, a teaching, a revelation, a tongue, an interpretation. Everything should build up others.

f.g: A hymn or song of praise.

f.w: Let all things be done unto edifying

n: If people speak in tongues, limit it to two or three, one at a time, with someone interpreting.
If there is no interpreter, the speaker should stay silent in the meeting and speak privately to God.

f.g: Don’t speak aloud in the meeting.

n: Let two or three prophets speak, and let others weigh what is said.
If someone seated receives a revelation, the first speaker should yield.
All can prophesy in turn so everyone learns and is encouraged.
Prophets remain in control of their spiritual gifts; true inspiration doesn’t force a person into uncontrolled behavior.
God is not a God of chaos but of peace — that is the pattern in all congregations.

f.w: God is not the author of confusion

n: Paul addresses a specific disorder involving women speaking in meetings. The JST changes “speak” to “rule,” suggesting the issue was authority over the meeting, not women’s participation — which Paul assumes elsewhere (11:5).

f.w: it is not permitted unto them to speak

n: Disruptive questions should be saved for discussion at home. Paul is addressing a local problem of order in that culture; the JST again reads “rule” for “speak.”

f.g: A remedy for disruptive questioning during worship.

n: Did God’s word originate with the Corinthians? Are they the only ones who received it? They should follow the practice of the wider Church.
Anyone who claims to be a prophet or spiritual should recognize that Paul’s instructions are the Lord’s commandments.
Whoever refuses to recognize this will not be recognized either.

f.g: Some manuscripts read “he is not recognized.”

n: So, brothers and sisters, eagerly seek prophecy, and don’t forbid speaking in tongues.
Do everything in a fitting and orderly way.
